story: AIDEA Houston land transfer ADL 234762, update of No.88. Forrer and Eastman sue on October 22nd, and Commissioner Crowther tells Senate Resources on October 26th that a decision before the December 7th inauguration is certainly possible

claims.claim: Eric Forrer and David Eastman filed their complaint against the land transfer on October 22nd, 2026.
claims.verbatim: Filed in the Trial Courts STATE OF ALASKA, FIRST DISTRICT AT JUNEAU OCT 22 2026
claims.source_outlet: Forrer and Eastman v. State of Alaska, complaint (Superior Court, Juneau)
claims.notes: Clerk's stamp, complaint p.1 (page image read by fact-checker). Signature block p.9 reads 'DATED this 22nd day of October 2026 at Juneau, Alaska.' Corroborated by Mat-Su Sentinel 'filed Thursday in Alaska Superior Court' (October 22nd, 2026 was a Thursday). The PDF is a 1-bit scan with no text layer; URL resolves (WebFetch confirmed %PDF header, Xerox scan).

claims.claim: The suit was filed in the Superior Court for the State of Alaska, First Judicial District at Juneau.
claims.verbatim: SUPERIOR COURT FOR THE STATE OF ALASKA FIRST JUDICIAL DISTRICT AT JUNEAU
claims.source_outlet: Forrer and Eastman v. State of Alaska, complaint (Superior Court, Juneau)
claims.notes: Caption, complaint p.1 and summons p.10. Mat-Su Sentinel and ADN both say Juneau Superior Court.

claims.claim: The case number is 1JU-26-01019 Civil.
claims.verbatim: 1JU-26-01019 Civil
claims.source_outlet: Forrer and Eastman v. State of Alaska, complaint (Superior Court, Juneau)
claims.notes: Printed '1JU-26-0' followed by HANDWRITTEN digits. p.1 reads 1JU-26-01019 with the last digits hand-filled; p.10 summons reads '1JU-26-0 1 019 Civil', consistent. Both pages agree on 01019. No news outlet prints the number, so it is single-sourced from a handwritten field; use it in small type or a citation, not as a headline figure.

claims.claim: The defendants are the State of Alaska, its Department of Natural Resources, and Governor Michael J. Dunleavy in his official capacity.
claims.verbatim: Governor Dunleavy is sued in his official capacity in order to obtain injunctive relief, as necessary.
claims.source_outlet: Forrer and Eastman v. State of Alaska, complaint (Superior Court, Juneau)
claims.notes: Complaint p.3 para 6. The p.1 caption misprints the agency as 'DEPARTMENT OF RESOURCES' (no 'Natural'); the summons p.10 is addressed to 'State of Alaska, Department of Natural Resources'. Do not reproduce the caption typo. Also note the counsel block misspells 'Davud Eastman'; do not quote it.

claims.claim: Juneau attorney Joseph W. Geldhof filed the complaint for the plaintiffs.
claims.verbatim: Law Office of Joseph W. Geldhof
claims.source_outlet: Forrer and Eastman v. State of Alaska, complaint (Superior Court, Juneau)
claims.notes: Letterhead p.1 (2 Marine Way, Juneau) and signature p.9. Mat-Su Sentinel 'by Joseph Geldhof, a Juneau-based attorney' corroborates.

claims.claim: The complaint says the transfer violates seven sections of the Alaska Constitution, namely Art. I Sec. 7, Art. VIII Secs. 2, 9, 10 and 17, and Art. IX Secs. 6 and 7.
claims.verbatim: including provisions contained in Art. I , Sec, 7, Art. VIII, Sec. 2, Art. VIII, Sec. 9, Art. VIII, Sec. 10, Art. VIII, Sec. 17, and Art. IX, Sec. 6 & 7.
claims.source_outlet: Forrer and Eastman v. State of Alaska, complaint (Superior Court, Juneau)
claims.notes: Complaint pp.1 to 2, para 1, quoted exactly including the filing's own stray spacing and comma ('Art. I , Sec, 7'). Count is 1 + 4 + 2 = 7. Independently corroborated by Mat-Su Sentinel 'The suit contends the transfer to AIDEA violates seven sections of the state constitution.' Caution for the deck: para 27 cites 'Art. XIII, Sections 9 and 10' (evidently a typo for VIII) and para 29 writes 'Sec. I, Art. 7' (inverted). Use the para 1 list only.

claims.claim: The land DNR proposes to convey is approximately 19,950 acres of state-owned land in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough.
claims.verbatim: proposes to convey approximately 19,950 acres (subject parcel) of State-owned land in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough
claims.source_outlet: Forrer and Eastman v. State of Alaska, complaint (Superior Court, Juneau)
claims.notes: Complaint p.5 para 16, repeated p.7 para 29. Matches DNR public notice ('approximately 19,950 acres') and the AIDEA fact sheet ('Approximately 19,950 acres'). Press rounds it: ADN 'roughly 20,000 acres', KTUU 'nearly 20,000 acres', Mat-Su Sentinel and ADN '30 square miles'. Sanity check: 19,950 / 640 = 31.2 square miles, so '30 square miles' is a fair round-down.

claims.claim: The parcel lies approximately two miles north of Houston, Alaska.
claims.verbatim: located within the Matanuska-Susitna Borough, approximately two miles north of Houston, Alaska.
claims.source_outlet: Forrer and Eastman v. State of Alaska, complaint (Superior Court, Juneau)
claims.notes: Complaint p.5 para 18. Same figure on DNR public notice ('approximately two miles north of Houston') and AIDEA fact sheet ('About 2 miles north of Houston').

claims.claim: The parcel sits within Township 18 North and Township 19 North of the Seward Meridian.
claims.verbatim: within Township 18 North, and Township 19 North, a geographical designation within the Seward Meridian.
claims.source_outlet: Forrer and Eastman v. State of Alaska, complaint (Superior Court, Juneau)
claims.notes: Complaint p.5 para 17, which also says the parcel is in 'DNR's Southcentral Region'. Useful for map placement; ranges are not given.

claims.claim: The complaint says DNR floated possible uses including data centers, advanced manufacturing, logistics hubs, utility development and gravel extraction.
claims.verbatim: including data centers, advanced manufacturing, logistics hubs, utility development, and gravel extraction, none of which are discussed in a meaningful factual level
claims.source_outlet: Forrer and Eastman v. State of Alaska, complaint (Superior Court, Juneau)
claims.notes: Complaint p.6 para 20. This is the plaintiffs' allegation and characterisation; attribute to the complaint. KTNA via Alaska Public Media (October 19th) independently lists 'Possible uses include data centers, utility development and gravel extraction.'
claims.suggested_phrasing: the complaint says DNR has floated uses including data centers

claims.claim: The complaint alleges a complete lack of analysis of the power and energy the development would require.
claims.verbatim: including the complete lack of analysis related to power and energy utilization required for development
claims.source_outlet: Forrer and Eastman v. State of Alaska, complaint (Superior Court, Juneau)
claims.notes: Complaint p.7 para 25. Allegation, attribute as such. Pairs with C47 (Ruaro, October 8th, no power source; data center implausible for lack of excess energy).

claims.claim: The complaint names three local bodies that voted to oppose the transfer, the Mat-Su Borough Assembly, the Houston City Council and the Meadow Lakes Community Council.
claims.verbatim: The Mat-Su Borough Assembly, the Houston City Council and the Meadow Lakes Community Council have voted to oppose the transfer of these public lands from DNR to AIDEA.
claims.source_outlet: Forrer and Eastman v. State of Alaska, complaint (Superior Court, Juneau)
claims.notes: Complaint p.8 para 31. COUNT DISCREPANCY, record both. The complaint names THREE. Mat-Su Sentinel names FOUR (see C24), adding the 'Willow Area Community Organization'. KTNA calls the Willow body the 'Willow Area Community Council' and says it sent a September resolution to the borough. If the deck gives a count, say which source it comes from.

claims.claim: The complaint says transferring the land to AIDEA without legislative authorization violates the separation of powers.
claims.verbatim: The transfer of these public lands to AIDEA without legislative authorization violates the separation of powers inherent in the Alaska Constitution and is against the public interest.
claims.source_outlet: Forrer and Eastman v. State of Alaska, complaint (Superior Court, Juneau)
claims.notes: Complaint p.8 para 33. Mat-Su Sentinel quotes the same phrase. Allegation.

claims.claim: The plaintiffs ask for an injunction barring DNR from transferring the land without a finding of legitimate public purpose and legislative authorization.
claims.verbatim: Injunctive relief, if necessary, precluding DNR from transferring public land to AIDEA without a finding of legitimate public purpose and adherence to constitutional standards and legislative authorization
claims.source_outlet: Forrer and Eastman v. State of Alaska, complaint (Superior Court, Juneau)
claims.notes: Complaint p.9, prayer for relief B (32 words). Prayer A seeks a declaration that the transfer 'represents an unconstitutional act by the executive branch of Alaska's state government' (p.8 to 9). The complaint seeks relief 'if necessary'; no injunction motion was seen.

claims.claim: The summons gives the State 40 days after receiving it to file an answer.
claims.verbatim: within 40 days after the day you receive this summons
claims.source_outlet: Forrer and Eastman v. State of Alaska, complaint (Superior Court, Juneau)
claims.notes: Summons p.10, addressed to the State of Alaska, Department of Natural Resources. The clock runs from SERVICE, and DNR said it had not been served as of Friday October 23rd (C22). Do not compute an answer due date from October 22nd.

claims.claim: Plaintiff Eric Forrer is a former University of Alaska regent who lives in Juneau.
claims.value: Regent of the University of Alaska
claims.verbatim: served as a Regent of the University of Alaska
claims.source_outlet: Forrer and Eastman v. State of Alaska, complaint (Superior Court, Juneau)
claims.notes: Complaint p.2 para 3 ('Forrer resides in Juneau, Alaska'). Mat-Su Sentinel 'longtime Juneau resident and former University of Alaska regent Eric Forrer'. Para 4 says Eastman 'has served as a member of the Alaska House of Representatives and resides in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough'; ADN calls him a 'Republican former state Rep.'

claims.claim: Forrer said of the suit, "We sued just to stop him."
claims.value: We sued just to stop him
claims.verbatim: We sued just to stop him.
claims.notes: Amy Bushatz, Mat-Su Sentinel, October 26th. Same text in the Alaska Public Media republication (October 27th, 8:22 AM AKDT): https://alaskapublic.org/news/economy/energy/2026-10-27/lawsuit-argues-houston-area-land-transfer-violates-alaska-constitution . That is a republication, NOT independent corroboration. 'Him' is Dunleavy. The plaintiff is an advocate; attribute plainly.

claims.claim: Forrer called the lawsuit a roadblock and a boulder in the road.
claims.verbatim: It's a roadblock
claims.notes: The page prints the full quote as 'It's a roadblock' + EM DASH + ' a boulder in the road.' The verbatim field is cut at the dash because house rules ban em dashes. If the slide quotes it, render as two quoted fragments ('a roadblock', 'a boulder in the road') or set it as two sentences with a disclosed edit. Never reintroduce the dash. Same text in the Alaska Public Media republication.

claims.claim: Forrer said the suit aims to stop Dunleavy from advancing the transfer before he leaves office in early December.
claims.verbatim: Forrer said the lawsuit aims to prevent Dunleavy from advancing the transfer before he leaves office in early December.
claims.notes: Alaska Public Media republication words it 'prevent Dunleavy from pushing it through before he leaves office in early December'. The exact date (December 7th) comes from ADN, C29.

claims.claim: Forrer said a 2018 suit he brought against a bond plan to pay oil tax credits ended with an Alaska Supreme Court ruling in his favor in September 2020.
claims.verbatim: The Alaska Supreme Court ultimately ruled in his favor in September 2020.
claims.notes: Sentinel context: then-Gov. Bill Walker's plan to 'sell up to $1 billion in bonds to pay tax credits' owed to oil companies. The court opinion itself was not fetched, so this rests on one outlet (republished by Alaska Public Media, not independent). Fine as attributed background.

claims.claim: Forrer said the dispute is not a right or left issue.
claims.value: not a right or left issue
claims.verbatim: This is not a right or left issue,
claims.notes: Sentinel says Forrer describes his views as 'left' and Eastman is a Republican. Also in the Alaska Public Media republication.

claims.claim: DNR declined to comment on the suit because it had not yet been served.
claims.verbatim: declined to comment Friday, saying they had not yet been served with the suit.
claims.notes: 'Friday' is October 23rd. Service status may have changed since. Write 'had not been served as of Friday'.

claims.claim: AIDEA is not a named party in the suit.
claims.verbatim: AIDEA officials declined to comment Friday because the agency is not a named party in the suit.
claims.notes: Confirmed against the primary. The complaint caption (p.1) names only the State, DNR and Dunleavy as defendants.

claims.claim: The Mat-Su Sentinel reports four local bodies have passed resolutions opposing the transfer, adding the Willow Area Community Organization to the three the complaint names.
claims.verbatim: Meadow Lakes Community Council and Willow Area Community Organization have passed resolutions opposing the transfer.
claims.notes: The full Sentinel list is the Mat-Su Borough Assembly, Houston City Council, Meadow Lakes Community Council and Willow Area Community Organization (the verbatim is the tail of a longer sentence). KTNA (C52) calls the Willow body the 'Willow Area Community Council' and describes a September resolution to the borough, so its exact name and action are inconsistent across sources. The complaint says three (C12). Safest copy is 'at least three local bodies', or name the source for the count.
claims.suggested_phrasing: four local bodies, according to the Mat-Su Sentinel

claims.claim: Reporting describes the parcel as 30 square miles of land abutting Houston, Willow and Meadow Lakes.
claims.verbatim: The proposed transfer would give 30 square miles of land abutting Houston, Willow and Meadow Lakes
claims.notes: Independent corroboration: ADN 'the 30-square-mile area' and Alaska Public Media October 15th 'about 30 square miles'. Primary figure is 19,950 acres (C07), about 31.2 square miles. Present 30 square miles as a rounded figure.

claims.claim: DNR Commissioner John Crowther appeared before the Senate Resources Committee after its members voted to subpoena him.
claims.verbatim: Crowther appeared before the Senate Resources Committee after its members voted to subpoena him earlier this month.
claims.notes: Margaret Carmel, ADN. The ADN page shows only 'Published: 1 day ago'; the Yahoo syndication https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/decision-land-transfer-mat-su-035900171.html is stamped Tuesday October 27th, 3:59 AM UTC (October 26th, evening, Anchorage), and the URL path is 2026/10/26. The subpoena vote is corroborated by Alaska Public Media October 15th (C44) and KTUU October 14th. No legislative video or minutes were fetched (akleg.gov 403 per scouts), so the testimony rests on ADN.

claims.claim: Crowther testified on Monday, October 26th.
claims.verbatim: On Monday, state lawmakers pressed Department of Natural Resources Commissioner John Crowther
claims.notes: The ADN body gives only 'Monday'; the photo caption reads 'Monday, Oct. 26, 2026.' Alaska Public Media October 15th said he 'would appear at a hearing on Oct. 26.' October 26th, 2026 is a Monday, so the sources agree.

claims.claim: Crowther said it was certainly possible the transfer could be approved before a new governor is sworn in.
claims.verbatim: he said it was "certainly possible" the transfer could be approved before a new governor is sworn in Dec. 7.
claims.notes: ADN also says 'Crowther declined to say exactly when the department will make a final decision'. Same wording on the Yahoo syndication. Only the two words 'certainly possible' are Crowther's direct quote; the rest is ADN paraphrase. Do not put the whole sentence in his mouth.
claims.suggested_phrasing: Crowther said approval before the inauguration was "certainly possible," ADN reported

claims.claim: A new governor is sworn in on December 7th.
claims.verbatim: well beyond the Dec. 7 inauguration
claims.notes: ADN gives the date twice ('sworn in Dec. 7', 'the Dec. 7 inauguration'); Yahoo syndication matches. A constitutional or Division of Elections source was not fetched. Days remaining are the showrunner's arithmetic and are not verified here.

claims.claim: Crowther said several steps will likely stretch the process beyond the inauguration and into the next governor's term.
claims.verbatim: Crowther noted there are multiple steps that will likely stretch out the process well beyond the Dec. 7 inauguration and into the new governor's term.
claims.notes: Two fragments the fetch tool returned as consecutive text, joined at 'inauguration' + 'and into'. ADN paraphrase, not a direct quote. Pair with C28 so the deck does not imply a decision on or before December 7th is likely.

claims.claim: The steps Crowther named include surveying the site and an appeal period.
claims.verbatim: That includes necessary due diligence on the site like surveying, as well as the appeal period
claims.notes: Consistent with the AIDEA fact sheet sequence (C40) and DNR notice appeal rule (C42). ADN adds 'Crowther also noted the ongoing lawsuit against the transfer and other legal avenues for the process to be challenged in court.'

claims.claim: Crowther also pointed to the ongoing lawsuit as a step that could prolong the process.
claims.verbatim: Crowther also noted the ongoing lawsuit against the transfer and other legal avenues for the process to be challenged in court.
claims.notes: Returned by the fetch tool as two consecutive fragments. ADN paraphrase.

claims.claim: DNR received more than 2,000 public comments on the transfer, which are still under review.
claims.verbatim: The Department of Natural Resources received more than 2,000 public comments about the project, which are currently under review as part of the transfer application process.
claims.notes: Single outlet (Yahoo is the same ADN story). The DNR notice does NOT state a count, and the 'more than 2,100' figure the brief raised appears on no fetched page (see killed). Use 'more than 2,000'.
claims.suggested_phrasing: more than 2,000 comments, according to the Anchorage Daily News

claims.claim: Anyone among the more than 2,000 commenters has standing during the appeal period to ask that the transfer be reconsidered.
claims.verbatim: during which any of the more than 2,000 people who submitted public comments on the transfer have standing to ask for the property change in ownership to be reconsidered.
claims.notes: Matches the primary rule on the DNR notice (C42) that only timely commenters may appeal. Note ADN says 'people' here and 'comments' in C33, which are not necessarily the same count. Keep that wording straight.

claims.claim: Crowther said using state land for development has been the governor's priority.
claims.verbatim: using our land for development has been the governor's priority
claims.notes: Direct quote. ADN: 'Crowther said in response to a question from Giessel about whether the proposal came at Dunleavy's request.' The page uses a curly apostrophe. Yahoo matches.

claims.claim: Earlier this year the Dunleavy administration changed a state regulation to allow a broader interpretation of what counts as a public purpose.
claims.verbatim: The Dunleavy administration earlier this year made a change to a state regulation that now allows for a broader interpretation of what constitutes a public purpose.
claims.notes: ADN's own reporting. The regulation text and its citation were not found by scouts or here, so there is no primary source. Attribute to ADN and do not name a regulation number or date.
claims.suggested_phrasing: the administration changed a regulation earlier this year to broaden what counts as a public purpose, ADN reported

claims.claim: Senate Resources Chair Cathy Giessel obtained DNR records on internal deliberations through a records request, and they were released with heavy redactions.
claims.verbatim: which were released with heavy redactions.
claims.notes: Full ADN sentence in fragments: 'Senate Resources Committee Chair Cathy Giessel, an Anchorage Republican, also filed a records request' / 'for Department of Natural Resources documents showing internal deliberations about the transfer' / 'which were released with heavy redactions.' The phrase 'heavily redacted' appears ONLY in a photo caption, not the body. KTUU October 14th independently says 'Sen. Cathy Giessel requested public records on the land transfer in Houston'.

claims.claim: Giessel said, "We are concerned that this is being urgently executed."
claims.verbatim: We are concerned that this is being urgently executed.
claims.notes: The passage opens '"The timing is of interest," Giessel said.' Yahoo syndication matches.

claims.claim: Sen. Bill Wielechowski said the broad reading of public purpose creates a giant loophole for AIDEA.
claims.verbatim: It seems like it creates this giant loophole for which AIDEA then has the ability to just go out and do whatever they want with the land in a way that DNR would not have the ability
claims.notes: 38 words, two consecutive fragments joined at 'go out' + 'and do'. ADN identifies him as one of the 'Anchorage Democratic Sens. Bill Wielechowski and Forrest Dunbar' who questioned Crowther. For a slide, the short form 'It seems like it creates this giant loophole' is safest.

claims.claim: Crowther told senators that what AIDEA could do with the parcel is quite broad.
claims.verbatim: what we would interpret AIDEA being able to do with this parcel is quite broad.
claims.notes: Direct quote fragment. Attribution to Crowther is from the fetch tool's summary of the page ('Crowther said AIDEA's authority to develop the land is "quite broad"').

claims.claim: AIDEA's transfer application lists secure, scalable data centers among the possible uses.
claims.verbatim: The possibilities include heavy and light industrial buildings, gravel mining, "secure, scalable data centers"
claims.notes: The preceding sentence: 'In its application to have the property transferred, AIDEA listed a range of possibilities that could be part of the development plans for the 30-square-mile area.' The application PDF (AIDEA_.810_Application_Complete_R.pdf, attached to the DNR notice) was not opened, so the phrase is verified only as ADN quotes it. The AIDEA fact sheet does not say 'data centers'; it lists 'utility, energy, and technology infrastructure' (C41b in notes of C39 below is not used).
claims.suggested_phrasing: AIDEA's application lists "secure, scalable data centers" among possibilities, ADN reported

claims.claim: A nonpartisan legislative attorney wrote a memo in September advising that the transfer may not be allowed under Alaska law.
claims.verbatim: His testimony came after a nonpartisan legislative attorney in September wrote a memo advising that the transfer may not be allowed under Alaska law.
claims.notes: Two consecutive fragments. The memo itself was not fetched, and it is a legal opinion, not a ruling.
claims.suggested_phrasing: a legislative attorney's memo said the transfer may not be allowed, ADN reported

claims.claim: Governor Dunleavy is term limited and cannot run for reelection.
claims.verbatim: Dunleavy is term limited from running for reelection.
claims.notes: ADN also reports that Dunleavy spokesperson Jeff Turner did not respond to a request for comment.

claims.claim: Republican candidate Dave Bronson said he was generally supportive of the transfer but noted DNR could scale down the 20,000 acres in its final approval.
claims.verbatim: he noted that 20,000 acres is the largest possible amount that could be transferred and that DNR could scale down the amount of land in its final approval.
claims.notes: Opening fragment: 'Former Anchorage Mayor Dave Bronson, one of three Republicans in the governor's race, said he was generally supportive of the proposal moving forward, but'. Candidate positions on the TRANSFER come from this ADN page only; the September 21st Beacon piece does not cover the transfer (see killed). Election-adjacent, so present all four candidates evenly.

claims.claim: Republican candidate Treg Taylor said he fully supports the transfer.
claims.verbatim: said in a short statement that he "fully supports the transfer."
claims.notes: ADN identifies him as 'Former Attorney General Treg Taylor, another GOP candidate in the race'.

claims.claim: Bernadette Wilson's campaign did not respond and Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins could not be reached about the transfer.
claims.verbatim: The race's only Democrat, Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, could not be reached for comment.
claims.notes: Wilson verbatim: 'Campaign staff for Bernadette Wilson, the third Republican gubernatorial candidate, did not respond for a request for comment.' Two candidates' silences in one claim; split if the deck uses them separately. Do not infer their positions on the transfer from their September data center positions (C55, C56).

claims.claim: The proposed conveyance rests on AS 38.05.810(a), the public and charitable use statute.
claims.verbatim: Statutory authority AS 38.05.810(a)
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (AIDEA)
claims.notes: Fact sheet p.1 table, confirmed visually from the PDF fetched today. The printed row continues with an em dash and 'Public and Charitable Use', cut here. The fact sheet is dated 'July 2026' with no day; 2026-07-01 is a placeholder for the month. It predates the window, so it is background-type context, but it is the agency's own document. The DNR notice body describes a 'noncompetitive public and charitable use conveyance' without citing .810 in the text.

claims.claim: AIDEA would make no payment for the value of the land but would cover administrative, survey, platting and closing costs.
claims.verbatim: AIDEA would make no payment for the value of the land, but remains responsible for administrative, survey, platting, and closing-related costs.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (AIDEA)
claims.notes: Fact sheet p.1. Table row: 'No payment for land value; AIDEA covers related costs'. Complaint calls it a transfer 'at no cost'. 'No cost' should be read as no payment for land value, not zero costs.

claims.claim: DNR proposes to waive the state's statutory reversionary interest in the land.
claims.verbatim: DNR proposes to waive the statutory reversionary interest, finding the waiver to be in the public interest.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (AIDEA)
claims.notes: Fact sheet p.1. A preliminary proposal, not final. Plain-language gloss for the deck: the land would not automatically return to the state if unused. That gloss is an inference from the term; keep it hedged.

claims.claim: The state would keep the mineral estate, including oil, gas, coal and geothermal resources.
claims.verbatim: The State retains oil, gas, coal, ore and other minerals, locatable minerals, fissionable material, geothermal resources, and fossils, along with access to explore and develop them.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (AIDEA)
claims.notes: Fact sheet p.1 under 'Mineral estate retained by the State.' Sand, gravel and rock are NOT reserved and 'may support AIDEA's development of the site'. That is why gravel extraction appears among uses. Existing oil and gas leases ADLs 394297 to 394302 remain.

claims.claim: AIDEA's fact sheet says no specific end use has been definitively selected for the land.
claims.verbatim: no specific end use has been definitively selected.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (AIDEA)
claims.notes: Fact sheet p.2. Scout D quoted it as 'no specific end use has been selected', which drops 'definitively'. Use the exact wording. Consistent with Ruaro's October 8th testimony (C57).

claims.claim: The fact sheet lists illustrative uses including rail-served logistics, utility, energy and technology infrastructure, advanced manufacturing and workforce housing.
claims.verbatim: Rail-served logistics and industrial uses; utility, energy, and technology infrastructure; advanced manufacturing; workforce housing; local material production; and stewardship / buffer areas.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (AIDEA)
claims.notes: Fact sheet p.2. The words 'data center' do NOT appear on the fact sheet. Data centers enter via the application as ADN quotes it (C41) and via the complaint (C10). Do not attribute 'data centers' to the fact sheet.

claims.claim: DNR must issue a Final Finding and Decision, and if it approves, survey, plat, title and closing steps must be completed before any conveyance.
claims.verbatim: If approved, survey, plat, title, and closing steps must be completed before any conveyance occurs.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (AIDEA)
claims.notes: Fact sheet p.2. Preceding bullet: 'DNR reviews timely comments and issues a Final Finding and Decision indicating whether the State intends to proceed.' Supports Crowther's point (C30, C31) that a decision before December 7th would not complete the conveyance.

claims.claim: DNR published the public notice on July 10th, 2026, and the comment period closed August 19th, 2026.
claims.verbatim: Comment Period Ends 5:00PM, Wednesday, August 19, 2026
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Natural Resources, Online Public Notices
claims.notes: Notice 'Proposed Land Conveyance to Alaska Industrial Development Export Authority near the city of Houston', Publish Date '7/10/2026', Department 'Natural Resources', case ADL 234762, approximately 19,950 acres. The fact sheet gives the same deadline. The notice states NO comment count. Year is in the claim because the period ended before this deck's frame; drop it in slide copy if the house date rule requires.

claims.claim: Only people who sent DNR timely written comment during the comment period can appeal the Final Finding and Decision.
claims.verbatim: Only persons from whom DNR DMLW LCS receives timely, written comment during the identified comment period will be eligible to file an appeal of the Final Finding and Decision or related actions.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Natural Resources, Online Public Notices
claims.notes: Two consecutive fragments joined at 'will be eligible' + 'to file an appeal'. Primary basis for ADN's 'standing' line (C34).

claims.claim: The Senate Resources Committee voted on Wednesday October 14th to subpoena Crowther, and he was set to appear at a hearing on October 26th.
claims.verbatim: would appear at a hearing on Oct. 26
claims.notes: Eric Stone, Alaska Public Media, October 15th, 5:06 PM AKDT (before the window, so background; it was No.88's material). Also 'voted Wednesday to issue a subpoena'. KTUU (Hannah Lee, updated October 14th) corroborates: 'The subpoena passed with five yays.' APM also reports the governor's office had not let Crowther attend an earlier October 8th hearing.

claims.claim: AIDEA Executive Director Randy Ruaro testified on October 8th that no developer, tenant, power source or site plan exists for the land.
claims.value: no developer, tenant, power source, or site plan
claims.verbatim: no developer, tenant, power source, or site plan exists for the land
claims.notes: Hannah Lee, KTUU, updated October 14th, 4:36 PM AKDT (URL path says 10/15). Fragment of a longer sentence. KTUU places it at the October 8th joint resources meeting. KTUU paraphrase of Ruaro, not a direct quote. Consistent with the AIDEA fact sheet 'no specific end use'.
claims.suggested_phrasing: Ruaro told lawmakers on October 8th that no developer, tenant, power source or site plan exists, KTUU reported

claims.claim: Ruaro called the rumored data center implausible because there is no excess energy supply.
claims.verbatim: the rumored data center is "implausible" because there is no excess energy supply.
claims.notes: Only 'implausible' is in quote marks. Independently corroborated by Alaska Public Media October 15th: AIDEA's executive director called hosting a data center on the site 'implausible'. Note the tension with C41 (application lists 'secure, scalable data centers'). That tension is real and sourced on both sides.

claims.claim: Giessel estimated the land is worth roughly $14 million a year in forgone revenue.
claims.verbatim: the land is worth roughly $14 million a year
claims.notes: A senator's back-of-envelope ESTIMATE, single outlet. KTUU: 'Giessel said the state would lose millions if the noncompetitive sale went through.' Method: the UA lease rate (C60) scaled to about 20,000 acres. Sanity check: 586,740 / 829 = about $708 per acre per year; times 19,950 = about $14.1 million. Arithmetic is consistent. The scaling assumes all acreage leases at a developed-parcel rate, which is generous. Must be framed as her estimate.
claims.suggested_phrasing: Giessel estimated the state could forgo roughly $14 million a year

claims.claim: Giessel said the University of Alaska charges a private Mat-Su developer $586,740 a year to lease 829 acres.
claims.verbatim: She said the University of Alaska charges a private Mat-Su developer $586,740 a year to lease 829 acres.
claims.notes: 'She' is Giessel (prior sentence). The UA lease document was not fetched. Single outlet.

claims.claim: KTNA reports the Houston City Council and Meadow Lakes Community Council voted unanimously in July to oppose the transfer.
claims.verbatim: The Houston City Council and Meadow Lakes Community Council voted unanimously to oppose the transfer back in July,
claims.notes: Marion Chesterton, KTNA, published by Alaska Public Media October 19th, 1:51 PM AKDT. The sentence continues 'according to reporting from the Mat-Su Sentinel', so it is second-hand. The same article says the Willow Area Community Council sent a September resolution opposing it.

claims.claim: Willow resident Ramey Smyth said the community needs air and water, which data centers are scheduled to contaminate.
claims.verbatim: We need air and water, which the data centers are scheduled to contaminate, and we don't need a whole lot else honestly.
claims.notes: Resident opinion, not a finding; no data center is planned (C51, C57). Use only as a voice, clearly attributed.

claims.claim: In September Bernadette Wilson said she would never allow Alaska to be littered with hyperscale data centers.
claims.verbatim: I will never allow Alaska to be littered with hyperscale data centers that take our resources and spoil our lands.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon via Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: James Brooks, Alaska Beacon, September 21st, republished by Alaska Public Media. Statement given by text. About data centers generally, NOT the Houston transfer.

claims.claim: In September Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins said he supports a moratorium on data center development in Alaska.
claims.verbatim: I support a moratorium on data center development in Alaska
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon via Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: Said at a September 8th forum per the Beacon. In the same piece Bronson said 'I'm a big believer in data centers' and Taylor said 'I think we need to embrace it'. All are data center positions, not transfer positions.

claims.claim: The Petersburg Borough Assembly voted 6-0 on October 5th to have the borough manager draft an ordinance for a nine-month moratorium on certain data center development.
claims.verbatim: In a 6-0 vote, members directed Borough Manager Steve Giesbrecht to draft an ordinance establishing a nine-month moratorium on certain data center development.
claims.notes: Orin Pierson, October 15th. Two fragments joined at 'ordinance' + 'establishing'. The meeting date sentence: 'The Petersburg Borough Assembly took two steps toward regulating data centers on Oct. 5.' The vote predates the window (October 5th) but the report is in window (October 15th). Article is paywalled after the opening; only the visible text is verified. Sponsor named as Vice Mayor Jeigh Stanton.

claims.claim: In a second 6-0 vote Petersburg directed the manager to draft Title 19 zoning amendments that address data centers.
claims.verbatim: In a second 6-0 vote, they directed him to begin drafting amendments to Title 19, the borough's zoning code, to address data centers specifically.
claims.notes: Two fragments joined. Single outlet, paywalled.

claims.claim: Neither Petersburg vote takes effect until the moratorium and zoning changes return as ordinances and pass three readings.
claims.verbatim: The moratorium and any zoning changes must each come back to the Assembly as ordinances and pass three readings.
claims.notes: Important hedge. Petersburg has NOT adopted a moratorium, only directed drafting.

claims.claim: Sitka city staff proposed a zoning code amendment that would define data centers and allow them by conditional use permit in five zoning districts.
claims.verbatim: allowing conditional use permits for data centers in the following zoning districts
claims.notes: Anna Laffrey, posted October 20th, 7:28 p.m. Also 'will consider a zoning code amendment that would define data centers'. The five districts as reported by the fetch tool: public lands, waterfront, industrial, general island, and the Gary Paxton special district. The count of five is the tool's tally, not a printed numeral; say 'several districts' unless re-checked. The definition sets no size threshold, so do not call it a 'micro' data center rule (see killed).

claims.claim: Four Sitkans had submitted comments on the amendment, and three asked for an outright ban on data center development.
claims.verbatim: Three people asked for an outright ban on data center development in Sitka.
claims.notes: Also 'four Sitkans had submitted public comments on the proposed zoning code amendment' (as of the Saturday before publication). A tiny sample. Do not present it as Sitka opinion.

claims.claim: The Sitka Planning Commission recommended prohibiting the construction of data centers, at least for now.
claims.verbatim: the Sitka Planning Commission recommended prohibiting the construction of data centers, at least for now.
claims.notes: KTOO newscast October 27th; action at 'a Wednesday meeting' (October 21st per the Sitka Sentinel's preview of a 7 p.m. Wednesday meeting). This goes beyond the staff proposal (C68), which would have allowed data centers by permit. It is a RECOMMENDATION. The Sentinel says an approved amendment would go to the Assembly for final approval; KTOO does not state the next step. Single outlet for the outcome.
claims.suggested_phrasing: Sitka's Planning Commission recommended a ban for now, KTOO reported; the Assembly has the final say

claims.claim: The Wrangell Borough Assembly unanimously voted down a land lease for a privately run data center on June 9th.
claims.verbatim: The borough assembly has unanimously voted down a proposed land lease for a privately run data center.
claims.notes: Wrangell Sentinel republished by KSTK, June 18th. Date sentence: 'The assembly on June 9 went with the manager's recommendation to retain the waterfront property'. Before the window, so background.

claims.claim: The rejected Wrangell application came from Greensparc, which sought to build a 10,000-square-foot facility.
claims.verbatim: recommended rejecting the lease application from Greensparc, which was looking to build a 10,000-square-foot facility
claims.notes: Site was borough land at the 6-Mile Mill deepwater port site. No megawatt figure given. Daily Sitka Sentinel (October 20th) also cites the 10,000-square-foot Wrangell proposal and names Greensparc as 'the Silicon Valley-based company Greensparc', with a 'modular 150-kW' unit installed in Cordova in 2024.

claims.claim: NOAA's Alaska Fisheries Science Center holds an archive of 2.5 million otolith pairs dating back to the 1960s.
claims.verbatim: an enormous archive of 2.5 million otolith pairs dating back to the 1960s.
claims.notes: NOAA feature, published September 28th, updated October 1st, so before the window. Archive is housed at the University of Washington Fish Collection (Burke Museum) per the page; the fetch tool's summary attributes the archive to AFSC's program, so phrase as 'an archive used by NOAA's Alaska Fisheries Science Center' if exact custody matters.

claims.claim: The otoliths in the archive come from 83 species.
claims.verbatim: 83 different species
claims.notes: Short fragment; the fetch tool says otoliths were gathered from 83 species over 40 years. Re-read the full sentence before a slide puts 'over 40 years' next to 'since the 1960s' (they look inconsistent; the 1960s date is about the archive, the 40 years about the collection effort).

claims.claim: NOAA scientists use Fourier Transform Near-Infrared Spectroscopy to streamline fish aging.
claims.verbatim: The technique uses Fourier Transform Near-Infrared Spectroscopy to streamline the aging process.
claims.notes: Corroborated by the October 7th leadership message (C78).

claims.claim: Machine learning algorithms correlate the otoliths' near-infrared spectral signatures directly to fish age.
claims.verbatim: machine-learning algorithms correlate directly to age
claims.notes: Fragment. The page also says scientists spent a decade training the models on tens of thousands of archive samples (fetch-tool paraphrase, not verbatim; do not quote).

claims.claim: NOAA says FT-NIR increases fish aging efficiency by 600 to 800 percent.
claims.verbatim: increases efficiency 600 - 800 percent
claims.notes: Appears in a PHOTO CAPTION, not the body, and the page renders it with a spaced hyphen. Agency self-report with no method given. Write it as 'six to eight times' only if hedged.
claims.suggested_phrasing: NOAA says the method raises efficiency 600 to 800 percent

claims.claim: Acting AFSC Director Jamal Moss wrote that the center couples FT-NIR with trained machine learning models to read otolith rings.
claims.verbatim: coupled with trained machine learning models to efficiently read otolith rings.
claims.notes: Leadership message by Dr. Jamal Moss, Acting Director, Alaska Fisheries Science Center, October 7th (before the window). The message does NOT mention staffing reductions (see killed).

claims.claim: Moss wrote that the more fish the center ages, the more accurate the data used in stock assessments.
claims.verbatim: the more fish we age, the more accurate the data used in stock assessments.
claims.notes: Also 'Increased sample throughput allows us to process more fish ages'.

stories_surviving: S1 AIDEA Houston land transfer ADL 234762, Forrer and Eastman suit and Crowther's October 26th testimony (64 verified claims, 20 primary)
S2 Southeast Alaska towns move to regulate data centers, Petersburg, Sitka and Wrangell (8 verified claims, none primary, all single-outlet local press)
S3 NOAA AFSC otolith aging with FT-NIR and machine learning (7 verified claims, all primary, all background because they predate the window)

killed.claim: DNR's public notice states more than 2,100 public comments were received.
killed.why: The DNR notice (id=224431) states no comment count. The only count on any fetched page is ADN's 'more than 2,000'. Use C33.

killed.claim: The September 21st Alaska Beacon piece reports the governor candidates' positions on the Houston land transfer.
killed.why: The Beacon page never mentions Houston or the transfer, only data centers generally. Transfer positions come from ADN October 26th (C44 to C46). Beacon data center positions are kept as background (C63, C64).

killed.claim: ADN's article body says the records were 'heavily redacted'.
killed.why: 'heavily redacted' appears only in a photo caption. The body says 'released with heavy redactions'. C37 uses the body wording.

killed.claim: Scout D wording that the AIDEA fact sheet says 'no specific end use has been selected'.
killed.why: Misquote. The fact sheet reads 'no specific end use has been definitively selected.' Corrected in C51.

killed.claim: The AIDEA fact sheet lists data centers among possible uses.
killed.why: The words 'data center' do not appear on the fact sheet, which says 'utility, energy, and technology infrastructure'. 'Secure, scalable data centers' is from the application as ADN quotes it (C41).

killed.claim: The DNR public notice cites AS 38.05.810 and describes the conveyance as no cost.
killed.why: The notice body does neither. It says 'noncompetitive public and charitable use conveyance'; '.810' appears only in attachment filenames. Statute and no-payment terms are sourced to the AIDEA fact sheet (C47, C48).

killed.claim: Petersburg's Assembly deadlocked 3-3 on a data center moratorium on September 21st.
killed.why: Not in the fetched Pilot article body. The only trace is a related-story headline ('proposal fails on 3-3 tie') with a URL dated September 24th. The article was not opened, and the date is unconfirmed.

killed.claim: Sitka, Petersburg and Wrangell are writing rules for 'micro' data centers.
killed.why: No fetched page uses 'micro' or sets a size threshold. Sitka's definition is size-neutral. The only sizes are Wrangell's 10,000-square-foot proposal and Cordova's 150-kW unit. Do not use 'micro' as a fact.

killed.claim: After the Sitka Planning Commission's recommendation the measure goes to the Assembly (as reported by KTOO).
killed.why: KTOO does not state a next step. The Daily Sitka Sentinel says an approved staff amendment would go to the Assembly; whether the commission's ban recommendation follows the same path is not on any page. Only the hedged phrasing in C70 survives.

killed.claim: Petersburg's proposed data center details, including Greensparc's role, size or power draw, per the Petersburg Pilot.
killed.why: Pilot article is paywalled after the opening paragraphs; none of this is visible. The Sitka Sentinel mentions a Greensparc 'small scale data center' proposal in Petersburg without size.

killed.claim: AFSC demographic or aging capacity is 'down 40%' (Foy, June 2025).
killed.why: Not on either fetched NOAA page, and the source was not supplied or fetched. Pre-window regardless.

killed.claim: The October 7th Moss leadership message discusses staffing reductions at AFSC.
killed.why: No sentence on the page mentions staffing reductions.

killed.claim: The complaint cites Art. XIII Sections 9 and 10 of the Alaska Constitution.
killed.why: Para 27 does print 'Art. XIII', but it is evidently a typo for Art. VIII, and it is not in the para 1 list of seven sections. Excluded so the deck does not report an eighth section or a nonexistent article reference.

killed.claim: Days remaining until the December 7th inauguration.
killed.why: Not verified by design. That is the showrunner's arithmetic on C29, per the brief.

killed.claim: Crowther's full testimony as shown in legislative minutes or video.
killed.why: No primary record reachable (akleg.gov returned 403 to scouts; no video found). All testimony claims rest on ADN and are marked non-primary.
